categories.category_explanation: Conditions confirming the perceptual availability and correct selection of task-relevant objects.

rules.generation_rule: Instantiate the predicate with all task-relevant objects the robot will interact with, using distinguishing non-spatial attributes for repeated object types.
Instantiate the predicate for the intended object immediately before its grasp, using a distinguishing non-spatial attribute when needed.

categories.category_explanation: Conditions confirming that the end effector has the required position and orientation before interaction.

rules.generation_rule: Instantiate the predicate for each object the robot newly grasps, pushes, or presses.
Instantiate <object> with each object the robot grasps.

categories.category_explanation: Conditions confirming the grasp, release, and contact states required by the action sequence.

rules.generation_rule: Instantiate the predicate for each object the robot grasps, using its unique task object name and verifying that the object is actually held.
prohibitions: Do not check the predicate as a precondition on the grasp waypoint.

rules.generation_rule: Instantiate the predicate for the object actually relinquished at each release waypoint.
Instantiate the predicate for each object the end effector contacts during a push waypoint.
prohibitions: Do not apply the precondition check to the first push waypoint of each contact-based manipulation run.

categories.category_explanation: Conditions confirming the task-specified qualitative relation between a released object and a named physical target.

rules.predicate_meaning: <object> rests on an upward-facing supporting surface of <target> (a table, shelf, tray, plate or lid), in stable contact and held up against gravity by that surface, and is no longer held by the gripper. It asserts support only, not containment.
rules.generation_rule: Instantiate on(object, target) for every release explicitly intended to leave the relinquished object supported on the named target.

rules.predicate_meaning: <object> has gone into the interior of <target> -- a container such as a box, drawer, basket, bin, bowl, cup or fridge -- and is not merely on its outer surface or rim.
rules.generation_rule: Instantiate inside(object, target) for each released object that the task explicitly requires to be placed inside a named target.

rules.predicate_meaning: <object> and <target> rest on the same supporting surface, adjacent to one another with no third object between them and separated by a gap small relative to the objects themselves. It asserts neither support of one by the other nor containment.
rules.generation_rule: Instantiate next_to(object, target) for each released object explicitly intended to be placed next to the named target.

rules.predicate_meaning: <object> is a door: a hinged or sliding panel that covers an opening in a fixed body (a door, a fridge/microwave/grill door, a box or toilet lid) and whose only two meaningful states are open and closed. The predicate holds when that panel is displaced from its frame far enough to leave the opening it covers accessible.
rules.generation_rule: Instantiate open(<object>) for each task-specified door the robot opens through non-grasping contact.

rules.predicate_meaning: <object> is a door: a hinged or sliding panel that covers an opening in a fixed body (a door, a fridge/microwave/grill door, a box or toilet lid) and whose only two meaningful states are open and closed. The predicate holds when that panel is fully seated against its frame, leaving the opening it covers not accessible.
rules.generation_rule: Instantiate the predicate for each task-specified door that the robot pushes closed.
